beginner_glossary.Back-end / advanced packaging: After chips are built on a silicon wafer (the 'front end'), the 'back end' cuts, stacks, bonds, and packages them. 'Advanced packaging' means high-tech ways of joining multiple chips very close together — essential for AI chips. ASMPT makes the machines that do this assembly.
beginner_glossary.SEMI segment: ASMPT's semiconductor-equipment business: die bonders, wire bonders, TCB tools, flip-chip and photonics bonders. Higher-margin, AI-leveraged.
beginner_glossary.SMT segment: Surface-Mount Technology: machines (e.g. SIPLACE pick-and-place) that place components onto printed circuit boards — used to assemble AI server boards, optical modules, and EV electronics. Lower-margin, higher-volume. ASMPT is reviewing strategic options for this segment.
beginner_glossary.TCB (Thermo-Compression Bonding): A bonding method using heat + pressure to attach chips with fine pitch — the workhorse for stacking AI logic and HBM. ASMPT is the volume leader in TCB by installed base.
beginner_glossary.Hybrid bonding: The most advanced bonding method: copper-to-copper fusion with no solder bumps, allowing the densest connections. Used for the highest-end 3D stacks; ASMPT participates but rival BESI is seen as the hybrid-bonding leader.
beginner_glossary.Chip-to-substrate (C2S) / chip-to-wafer: Two TCB configurations: C2S bonds a die onto a package substrate; C2W bonds a die onto another wafer/interposer. C2W is needed as chips move from single-die (SoC) to multi-chiplet (SoIC) designs.
beginner_glossary.Fluxless / AOR / plasma bonding: Advanced TCB techniques that avoid chemical 'flux' (which leaves residue). Cleaner, higher-precision bonding required for the finest pitches and HBM. ASMPT won orders for fluxless plasma-based AOR (Assembly-on-Reflow) C2W tools.
beginner_glossary.HBM (High-Bandwidth Memory): Memory chips stacked vertically (e.g. 8/12/16-high) next to an AI processor for huge data speed. HBM4 16-high stacks need advanced TCB/hybrid bonding — a major growth driver.
beginner_glossary.CPO (Co-Packaged Optics): Putting the optical (light) engine right next to the compute chip instead of in a separate pluggable. Needs ultra-precise bonding of fiber arrays, microlenses, and photonic/electronic ICs — a new market for ASMPT from ~2028.
beginner_glossary.Optical transceiver (800G / 1.6T): Modules that convert electrical signals to light for fast data-center networking. As speeds rise (400G->800G->1.6T) more precise assembly is needed. ASMPT calls itself the market leader and won 1.6T bulk orders.
beginner_glossary.Bookings / book-to-bill: Bookings = value of new orders received. Book-to-bill = bookings divided by revenue; above 1.0 means orders are growing faster than sales (a positive leading indicator). ASMPT SEMI book-to-bill was 1.13 in Q1 2026.
beginner_glossary.Adjusted (non-HKFRS): Company-defined profit that strips out one-time items (e.g. disposal gains, restructuring). ASMPT reports both statutory (HKFRS) and 'adjusted' figures; adjusted better reflects ongoing operations.
beginner_glossary.Continuing vs discontinued operations: After deciding to sell a business (here, NEXX), accounting splits results into 'continuing' (the kept business) and 'discontinued' (the part being sold). This makes year-over-year profit comparisons tricky.
beginner_glossary.Gross margin: Revenue minus the direct cost of making the product, as a % of revenue. ASMPT's group GM (~38-40%) is lower than pure die-bonder peers because of the high-volume SMT mix.
beginner_glossary.P/E ratio: Price-to-Earnings: share price divided by earnings per share. A high P/E means investors pay a lot today for expected future profit growth.

company_snapshot.what_it_is: ASMPT Limited is one of the world's largest suppliers of back-end semiconductor assembly and packaging equipment, plus surface-mount (SMT) machines for circuit-board assembly. In the AI supply chain it sits in the packaging tier, selling TCB, die/wire bonders, flip-chip, and photonics tools to foundries, OSATs (outsourced assembly/test houses), IDMs, and memory makers. It is the volume leader in thermo-compression bonding (TCB) by installed base and a leader in optical-transceiver assembly.
company_snapshot.headquarters: Singapore (principal HQ); listed and co-headquartered in Hong Kong (HKEX); incorporated in the Cayman Islands.
company_snapshot.founder_ceo: Robin Ng (Robin Gerard Ng Cher Tat) — Group CEO since May 2020 (~6 years; 17+ years at ASMPT) (ASMPT leadership page, 2026).
company_snapshot.founded: 1975 (as ASM Pacific Technology; renamed ASMPT Limited in June 2022).
company_snapshot.manufacturing_footprint: Manufacturing and R&D across China (notably), Singapore, Malaysia, Germany (SMT/SIPLACE heritage), and other Asian sites; serves a global OSAT/IDM/foundry customer base. ~11,300 employees (2022 figure; current headcount not disclosed in sources).

business_model.summary: ASMPT makes money by selling capital equipment (machines) used to assemble and package semiconductors (SEMI segment) and to mount components onto circuit boards (SMT segment), plus recurring spares, service, and consumables. It is highly cyclical and AI-leveraged: when chipmakers and electronics makers expand capacity, ASMPT's orders surge with strong operating leverage; in downturns, profits fall sharply. The company is actively narrowing its focus toward higher-value back-end packaging (it divested NEXX and is reviewing strategic options for the SMT business).
how_they_make_money: SEMI segment (higher margin): TCB tools (logic and HBM), high-end die bonders, wire bonders, flip-chip, and photonics bonders for optical transceivers and CPO.
SMT segment (higher volume, lower margin): SIPLACE pick-and-place lines that assemble AI server boards, optical modules, and EV electronics. Under strategic review.
Recurring revenue: spare parts, service, upgrades, and consumables across a large installed base (e.g. 500+ TCB tools).
Pricing/mix leverage: gross margin swings with the SEMI-vs-SMT mix (SEMI ~46% GM in Q1 2026 vs blended group ~39.5%).
competitive_moat_analyst_view: ANALYST VIEW: Largest TCB installed base in the world (500+ tools), giving scale, process know-how, and a service annuity — a durable edge as TCB demand grows with AI.
ANALYST VIEW: Breadth across the entire back-end flow (TCB, die/wire bond, flip chip, photonics, CPO, SMT) lets it capture demand wherever AI packaging complexity rises.
ANALYST VIEW: Leading position in optical-transceiver assembly (claimed market leader; 1.6T bulk orders) and early, multi-player CPO engagement across all four high-precision bonding steps.
ANALYST VIEW: Industry recognition (Intel EPIC Supplier Award 2026) and engagement with the largest memory player on a process-standard evaluation could entrench it in HBM.

revenue_streams.analyst_view: ANALYST VIEW: ASMPT is a two-engine business riding AI from both sides — SEMI (high-margin packaging tools) and SMT (high-volume AI server-board assembly). The Q1 2026 order surge (group book-to-bill well above 1) signals a strong upcycle, with SEMI margins recovering as TCB/AI mix rises. The strategic review of SMT suggests management wants to become a purer, higher-margin back-end packaging play; the key uncertainty is timing and the pace at which HBM TCB orders convert.

competitors.landscape_summary: ASMPT competes in back-end (assembly/packaging) and SMT equipment. The high-end bonding battleground — TCB and hybrid bonding — is led by ASMPT, BESI, and Kulicke & Soffa, with Hanmi Semiconductor and Hanwha strong in HBM-specific TCB and Applied Materials relevant in process steps and integrated lines. ASMPT positions as the TCB volume leader; BESI is regarded as the hybrid-bonding precision leader.

key_competitors.note: Hybrid-bonding leader with sub-micron precision for HBM4 16/24-high stacking; ASMPT and BESI both gaining share from Korean suppliers. BESI leads ultra-high-end hybrid bonding; ASMPT leads TCB by installed base.
Korea-based leader in HBM 'dual-TC' bonding; eyeing first TC-bonder deliveries for new formats (e.g. HBF) in 2H26; a key threat in the memory/HBM TCB sub-segment.
Wire-bonding/die-bonding heritage; mid-range in advanced packaging; developing hybrid bonding (CuFirst with ROHM).
Broad front-end/process player; relevant in hybrid-bonding process steps and integrated assembly lines; partner/competitor rather than direct die-bonder rival.

competitors.differentiation_analyst_view: ANALYST VIEW: ASMPT's edge is scale and breadth — the largest TCB installed base (500+ tools), full back-end coverage, and leadership in optical-transceiver assembly. Its main competitive risks are (1) BESI/Hanmi winning the highest-value HBM hybrid-bonding sockets, and (2) the lower-margin SMT mix diluting group profitability until the strategic review resolves. The race for the largest memory player's process-standard qualification is a key swing factor.
facts: FACT (2026-04-22): ASMPT targets 35-40% of the TCB market (USD 1.6B TAM by 2028); reinforced C2S TCB leadership and won 4 C2W fluxless tools.
FACT (2026, industry): ASMPT has the largest TCB installed base worldwide (500+ tools); ASMPT and BESI gaining HBM-bonding share from Korean suppliers.
FACT (2026-04-22): A key memory player is qualifying ASMPT's fluxless AOR solution for HBM4 16-high; ASMPT is finalizing an evaluation program with the biggest memory player.

valuation.analyst_view: ANALYST VIEW: ASMPT is a high-quality, AI-leveraged packaging leader trading at a demanding valuation. After a ~3x run in a year, the stock sits ABOVE most published analyst targets and at ~58-67x forward/trailing earnings (much higher on recurring profit). That only makes sense if the AI packaging upcycle drives a multi-year earnings ramp — plausible given record bookings and TCB leadership, but with real timing risk around HBM TCB orders, SMT margin dilution, and cyclicality. This is an opinion, not a recommendation.

final_research_summary.one_paragraph: ASMPT is one of the world's largest back-end semiconductor assembly and SMT equipment makers and the volume leader in TCB (thermo-compression bonding), squarely leveraged to AI packaging. The facts are strong: Q1 2026 group revenue USD 507.9M (+32% YoY) and bookings USD 727.0M (+71.6% YoY) were multi-year highs, with SEMI margins recovering and photonics revenue up ~5x. But what is being PRICED is a multi-year AI packaging boom: at HKD 208.80 the stock has risen ~3x in a year, trades above most analyst targets, and sits at ~58-67x forward/trailing earnings (far higher on recurring profit, since FY2025 adjusted net profit was only HK$466.7M). The investable question is the pace and durability of HBM TCB orders and the SMT restructuring — high-probability in direction, uncertain in timing. No buy/sell/hold call is offered. (Currency note: revenue in USD; profit/EPS/dividend/price in HKD.)
